chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Hamza, from Ibrahim ibn Hilal, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A goblet containing gold and silver, can I buy it with gold or silver?' He said: 'If you are able to purify it, then no (do not buy), and if you are not able to purify it, then there is no problem (you may buy).'
ai.seo_question: Can I buy a gold and silver mixed goblet with gold or silver money?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the rules of *Riba al-Fadl* (excess in exchange) regarding mixed-metal vessels, establishing that the prohibition applies only when the components can be distinguished and separated. The Imam’s ruling highlights the practical principle that if the gold and silver are inextricably mixed such that they cannot be purified, the transaction is permissible, avoiding the strictness of the prohibition. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*Yusr*) in commercial transactions when the condition for *Riba*—the ability to distinguish and equalize specific commodities—is not met.
